hints: The removals array gives a current one-based rank, not an original position.
Store 1 for each still-present list element and 0 for removed elements in a Fenwick tree.
Select the k-th live element by prefix counts, output its value, and remove its marker.
analogy: A Fenwick tree lets you find the k-th remaining item even as earlier items disappear.
example: From [2,6,1,4], removing rank 2 removes 6; the remaining list is [2,1,4].
algorithm: Initialize all Fenwick positions to 1. For each rank k, binary-lift to find the smallest index with prefix count at least k, output its original value, then add -1 at that index.
correctness: The prefix count is the number of live elements up to each position, so selecting its kth threshold returns precisely the kth surviving item.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
